questions.question: What are Rails environments and how do they differ?
questions.title: Rails Environments
questions.direct_answer: Rails has three built-in environments: development (your laptop; code reloads on every request, verbose logs, no caching), test (for the test suite; isolated DB, fast), production (optimized; code preloaded, caching on, assets compiled, compressed logs). You set it with RAILS_ENV=production (or --environment) when running commands, and each has its own config in config/environments/development.rb etc. and its own database in config/database.yml. The environment controls behavior: development favors debugging, production favors speed. Gems can be grouped to an environment (group :development do gem 'pry' end) so they don't load in prod.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know the three environments (development/test/production) and how they differ (reload/caching/config), and how to set RAILS_ENV.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Running prod settings in dev (caching hides bugs) or forgetting RAILS_ENV when running a migration in prod.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Three envs: development (reload, verbose), test (isolated, fast), production (caching, compiled). Set with RAILS_ENV; each has its own config and DB.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Rails has three environments: development, test, production.
Development: reloads code, verbose logs, no caching (for debugging).
Production: caching on, assets compiled, code preloaded, compressed logs (for speed).
Set the environment with RAILS_ENV=production (or -e); each has its own config and DB.
Group dev/test gems (group :development) so they don't load in production.

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: Rails has three built-in environments. Development is your laptop: code reloads on every request, logs are verbose, and caching is off, so you can debug. Test is for the test suite: an isolated database and fast boot. Production is optimized: code is preloaded, caching is on, assets are compiled, and logs are compressed. You set it with RAILS_ENV equals production, or the environment flag, when running commands, and each has its own config in config slash environments and its own database in config slash database dot yml. The environment controls behavior: development favors debugging, production favors speed. Gems can be grouped to an environment — group development do gem pry end — so they don't load in production. A common mistake is running production settings in development, because caching hides bugs while you code, and forgetting RAILS_ENV when running a migration.

#   RAILS_ENV=production rails db:migrate

# Each has its own config file:
#   config/environments/development.rb   (reload, verbose logs, no cache)

#   config/environments/production.rb     (caching, eager load, compressed logs)
